Questions to ask together

Every question here can be asked aloud by a family, a study circle or a class.

Ground rules

  1. One person reads the question. Everyone answers for themselves first, in silence or in writing.
  2. No answer is wrong. Ask what follows from it, not whether it is right.
  3. Read the verse aloud once, with its source. Let it sit before anyone comments.
  4. Nobody has to say what they believe. Passing is always allowed.

Choose a question

The ground

  • Why is there anything at all, instead of nothing?
  • If everything needs a maker, who made God?
  • Is there a sign of God inside a person too?
  • If reason evolved only to keep us alive, why trust it about truth?
  • Is hurting a child wrong even if everyone approved?
  • Has science made belief in God unnecessary?
  • What evidence would be enough to believe?
  • If God wants people to believe, why doesn't He just appear?
  • How can a good God allow children to suffer?
  • If there is no God, can a life still mean anything?
  • What were we made for?
  • Why one God, not many gods or a blind force?
  • Is there one God behind all the names?
  • Is the true God beyond what people worship?
  • Did the Buddha point to what is never born?
  • What can a person lean on that will never fade?
  • Is anyone really listening, or is it a feeling?
  • Who carries the burden of proof: the one who asks, or the one who makes the claim?
  • Did religion just evolve in the human brain?
  • Why would a perfect being need worship?
  • Isn't morality just something humans made up?
  • Does God command what is good, or make it good?
  • How can anyone tell for themselves what is true?
  • How much of what we know has anyone checked for themselves?
  • Can many weak arguments add up to anything?
  • Could the universe simply be there, with no reason at all?
  • Is human dignity real, or only something we agreed on?
  • Does believing in revelation mean switching off reason?
  • Why would a holy book ask for evidence? Isn't faith supposed to need none?
  • How sure does a person need to be before believing?
  • Is it shameful for a refugee to need help?
  • How can a person live with worry about the future?
  • How can a mind that will not stop find rest?
  • Why would a merciful God allow suffering?
  • Is there wisdom in hardship, or is that only something people say?
  • Why doesn't God stop people from doing harm?
  • Why do good people suffer?
  • Is an earthquake a punishment, and what of those who die?
  • What is patience, and what is it not?
  • Is gratitude something we owe, or only something we feel?
  • Does God give reasons for His commands?
  • Is good only good because God says so?
  • What makes a human life sacred?
  • Must a person give up remembering their ancestors?
  • Should we understand life before we ask about death?
  • Can words about God ever be true to Him?
  • When thanks are given at a shrine at New Year, who is thanked?
  • Is it wrong to make a vow for someone who is sick?
  • Were the spirits that troubled a person real?
  • Is poverty a sign of weak faith?
  • Is it honest to pray when unsure about believing?
  • What would faith change in an ordinary week?
  • School denies God, grandfather fasts. Who is right?
  • Can faith be honest about what it does not yet know?
  • Can a person take their time deciding about faith?
  • Why is it so hard to stop scrolling a phone?

One nation

  • Are all humans really one family?
  • Does any race or nation stand higher with God?
  • If humanity is one family, why are people so different?
  • Does Adam's sin pass to his children?
  • Why do people pray in emergencies, even those who say they don't believe?
  • How can anyone trust God after harm done in His name?

One order

  • Did God send anyone to every people, or only to the Middle East?
  • What exactly was every messenger told to say?
  • Why did four prophets begin with the same words?
  • Did Muhammad bring a new religion?
  • Which commandment did Jesus call the first?
  • How did every nation learn what God asks?
  • Why do Sikhs and the Quran both say God is One?
  • Why does this app quote the Torah, Psalms and Gospel?
  • What do the earlier scriptures and the Quran share?
  • Did Abraham and Moses teach what the Quran does?
  • Were Noah, Moses and Jesus given one command?
  • Why do the Quran's commands match the Torah's and the Gospel's? Is it one source?
  • Did God hear the old prayers, by the name a people knew?

One religion

  • Is living by God's will the same as surrender?
  • What does "Islam" actually mean in the Quran?
  • Why call it Islam if earlier prophets came first?
  • Was Abraham a Jew, a Christian or a Muslim?
  • If the laws differ, is it really the same religion?
  • What about people who never heard the message?

People divided

  • Who first drew the lines between religions?
  • If God wanted one religion, why are there so many?
  • Is all disagreement bad?
  • Who actually split the religions, and why?
  • Hasn't religion caused most wars?
  • If faiths share so much, why do people fight?

Why they divided

  • What does it mean to make desire a god?
  • How can anyone tell their opinions from their ego?
  • Isn't organised religion just a way of controlling people?
  • Do people believe what they believe only because of their parents?
  • Born elsewhere, a person would believe something else. Does that make it all culture?

Each party content

  • Who is meant by “each party proud of its own”?
  • Could the verse on rival groups describe anyone today?
  • Is any group the saved group?
  • What proof does anyone have for their path, other than being raised in it?
  • Why are religious people sometimes the worst?
  • Can a person be sure they are right and respect others?

The way back

  • Whom did Jesus teach his disciples to pray to?
  • Does God hear a person who calls on Him directly?
  • Can a person speak to God directly?
  • Asked about God, why is the answer so direct?
  • How near is God?
  • Why does God not answer some prayers?
  • Does God hear a person even if they are a sinner?
  • What can Muslims, Jews and Christians agree on?
  • How can a person cope with loneliness in a new city?
  • How can parents live with fear for their child?

The path

  • What would a real message from God have to look like?
  • What is the Straight Path, actually?
  • Did Jesus really say "this is a straight path"?
  • How does the Quran honour Mary?
  • Who was Muhammad, and why believe him?
  • Why does the Quran correct its own Prophet?
  • Did Muhammad copy from Jews and Christians?
  • Could Muhammad read?
  • Why was the Quran in Arabic, and is a translation enough?
  • Is Muhammad foretold in the Bible?
  • Whose path is asked for in every prayer?
  • Why trust a book written 1,400 years ago?
  • Are the Quran's "scientific miracles" real?
  • Why believe a miracle story from long ago?
  • Where did a man with no books get the Quran?
  • Where did the stories of the earlier prophets in the Quran come from?
  • Did the Arabs know the Quran's stories before it came?
  • What does Muhammad's life before age 40 show?
  • Did someone secretly teach Muhammad the Quran?
  • If all prophets said the same, what follows for a person?
  • Why does the Quran appeal to Jewish scholars?
  • How could anyone tell a true messenger from a false one?
  • Can a religion be judged by how its people act?
  • Is there a test of a prophet that Jews, Christians and Muslims could all accept?
  • Could a sincere person be wrong about hearing from God?
  • What would it even mean for a book to be from God?
  • Is the challenge to match the Quran a fair test?
  • Why does the Quran keep asking people to think instead of simply telling them what to believe?
  • Is faith a blind leap, or based on what a person sees?
  • Did the Quran truly foretell Rome's victory?
  • Did the Quran foretell one man's unbelief?
  • Is today's Quran the same as the Prophet's?
  • What do the oldest Quran manuscripts show, and do they match the text we read today?
  • Do the Quran's many readings mean different versions?
  • Over 23 years, did the Quran contradict itself?
  • How did the Quran's first listeners react?
  • What does the Quran say about the orphan, the poor and the baby girl?
  • Must a person be fair even to people they dislike?

Stewardship

  • Does God want sacrifices, or a good heart?
  • Why are we on this earth?
  • What is the role on earth of someone with an ordinary job?
  • Can ordinary work be worship?
  • Does the Quran say anything about caring for the earth?
  • Must a person stand for justice even against their own family?
  • Is anyone's wealth really their own?
  • What is owed to the poor?
  • How should people of different faiths treat one another?

The scale

  • What happens when a person dies?
  • How could bones and dust live again?
  • Has anyone ever seen something dead come back?
  • Is death like falling asleep?
  • Why would there be a judgment at all?
  • Do those who escape justice ever answer for it?
  • Does God forgive freely when a person returns?
  • Is repentance enough without a sacrifice?
  • If karma loses no deed, who keeps the record?
  • Does karma work like gravity, or like a judge?
  • Must a person purify themselves, or can another?
  • What is weighed on the Day of Judgment?
  • Does a small deed count?
  • Will anyone stand with a person on Judgment Day?
  • Why test people instead of simply making them good?
  • How does a person forgive someone who hurt them?
  • What are life's tests and trials really for?
  • Why do people long for justice, even when it never comes?
  • Can medicine explain everything about death?
